title: File:A dim airglow blankets Earth’s horizon as a faint Moon sets above the Indian Ocean (iss074e0342246).jpg
artist: NASA Johnson Space Center
description: iss074e0342246 (Feb. 22, 2026) --- A dim airglow blankets Earth’s horizon as a faint Moon sets above a dark and vast Indian Ocean. The International Space Station was orbiting 265 miles above the Seychelles—an East African archipelago nation of 115 islands—at approximately 11:08 p.m. local time when this photograph was taken. Credit: NASA/Chris Williams

title: File:A faint airglow blankets Earth's horizon above the Pacific Ocean (iss073e0780028).jpg
artist: NASA Johnson Space Center / Jonny Kim
description: iss073e0780028 (Sept. 2, 2025) --- A faint airglow blankets Earth's horizon in this photograph taken from the International Space Station as it orbited 259 miles above the Pacific Ocean between Hawaii and California. This natural glow is produced when solar ultraviolet radiation excites oxygen molecules in the upper atmosphere during the day, which then release that energy as visible light at night.

title: File:Earth's thin blue atmosphere traces the planet's horizon above the Pacific Ocean (iss074e0089803).jpg
artist: NASA Johnson Space Center
description: iss074e0089803 (Jan. 16, 2026) --- Earth's thin blue atmosphere traces the planet's horizon as the sun's glint beams off a partly cloudy Pacific Ocean west of Chile on the South American continent. The International Space Station was orbiting 271 miles above Earth at the time of this photograph.

title: File:Iss064e006316 (Nov 21, 2020) --- Earth's limb, or horizon, is pictured from the International Space Station as it orbited above the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Chile.jpg
artist: NASA Johnson Space Center
description: iss064e006316 (Nov. 21, 2020) --- Earth's limb, or horizon, is pictured from the International Space Station as it orbited above the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Chile. Framing the top of the photograph, is a portion of Japan's Kibo laboratory module with its Exposed Facility that houses external experiments to understand the effects of space radiation and extreme temperatures on a variety of materials.
